LESSON: SIGN READING 11.2.1 EXTENSIVE SIGN READING: FICTION

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.2: Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Which story books or plays have you read? • What makes a book interesting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of vocabulary related to the theme for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. distinguish between fiction and non-fiction reading materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. select and sign read grade appropriate fiction materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. keep a portfolio of the subject matter,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the importance of reading fiction for exposure. • In groups or pairs, learner is guided to observe, fingerspell and sign words related to the theme, • Individually, learner is guided to research on the differences between fiction and non-fiction materials and give examples of each. • Individually, learner is guided to sign read self-selected fiction materials and use a graphic organizer to write short summaries of the subject. • In groups, learners are guided to make a readers’ gallery by displaying the material sign read with a caption indicating its subject matter. • Individually, learner is guided to take photos of their display and keep a soft and hard copy of the photo in their portfolio or, write a card with the title and the subject matter of the material read and keep it in their portfolio. • Which story books or plays have you read? • What makes a book interesting? 136 • In groups, learners are guided to discuss why reading fiction materials is important.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Sign Reading 11.2.1 Extensive Sign Reading: Fiction together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving researching skills when the learner research from different sources the difference

between fiction and non-fiction materials.

• Digital Literacy: skill of interacting with technology when learners capture images of the readers galleries and keep them in

their digital portfolio.

Values:
Respect: the learners recognise the value of each other’s contribution in building the readers’ gallery.

Link to other subjects

The learner is able to relate reading skills to nurture a reading culture and promote discipline required in reading fiction materials

in Kiswahili.

Suggested Learning Resources

Word cards, Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g. tablets and mobile phones,

and books, E-books, Internet, Online dictionaries, Digital story books, Projector, digital devices.
